messages:
alex: quick thread to land span-name + semantic attr guidance for inference pipeline (router -> runtime -> kv-cache -> postprocess). thinking we need a low-cardinality span.name scheme + richer attributes for model/tokens/cache. initial proposal below, open to pushback

maya: love it. can you sketch concrete examples? curious whether model/version should be in span name or attrs

alex: sketch: prefer generic span names and put model/version in attributes. sample names:
- llm.request (root for incoming request handling)
- llm.router.route (router logic + policy decision)
- llm.runtime.generate (actual autoregressive generation)
- llm.kvcache.lookup (cache attempt)
- llm.kvcache.populate (writing to cache)
- llm.postprocess (filtering/formatting)

dheeraj: agreed on keeping model out of name. putting model in name causes cardinality explosion for exporters. attributes to capture model metadata and token counts instead.

sasha: what about multi-stage spans (batching vs single-request)? should we add "/batch" suffix?

alex: prefer one span.name for the logical operation and attach an attribute `batch.size` (int) when relevant. avoids combinatorial names. e.g. llm.runtime.generate + batch.size=8

maya: ok. attribute naming conventions? snake_case vs dot.delimited? kebab?

alex: propose dot.delimited lower_case, consistent with OTEL semantic conventions. examples: 
```
model.name: string  # e.g., gpt-4o-mini, llama-3-13b
model.revision: string  # pinned model revision or checksum
model.variant: string  # quantization, e.g., int8, fp16
inference.kind: string  # generation | embeddings | rerank
tokens.prompt: int
tokens.completion: int
tokens.total: int
kvcache.hit: bool
kvcache.entries: int
route.decision: string  # e.g., fallback, pin_to_dedicated, fallback_to_hosted
route.tier: string  # hosted | dedicated | private
request.id: string  # internal request id
response.size_bytes: int
latency.ms: int
```

dheeraj: important: do NOT put any prompt text in attributes or tags. only token counts. PII risk + cardinality.

sasha: export concerns: high-cardinality attrs like model.revision or request.id should be marked as "sensitive/high-card" and not exported to long-term storage by default. we need an exporter filter config.

alex: agreed. proposal: default export set includes low-cardinality attrs (model.name, model.variant, inference.kind, kvcache.hit, tokens.total, latency.ms). high-cardinality: model.revision, request.id -> kept in short-term retention (7d) only and redacted for long-term. otel-bot: note retention policy configured: traces.short_term.ttl=7d, traces.long_term.ttl=90d

maya: sampling strategy? big requests with many tokens are expensive to store. maybe bias sampling toward high-cost requests for troubleshooting.

alex: yes — sampling weights: base_weight=1, plus weight += tokens.total/1000, plus weight += (kvcache.hit ? -0.5 : 1.0) so cache misses sampled more. include a flag attr `sample.reason` when selected (e.g., heavy_tokens, cache_miss, manual)

dheeraj: small nit: attribute names shouldn't collide with existing observability keys. maybe prefix with `llm.`? e.g., llm.tokens.total vs tokens.total. Thoughts?

sasha: prefix reduces collision but more verbose. we already use `route.*` and `kvcache.*`. keeping consistent top-level `llm.` might help. maybe only prefix model and tokens: llm.model.name, llm.tokens.*.

alex: updated minimal set w/ llm prefix: 
```
llm.model.name
llm.model.variant
llm.inference.kind
llm.tokens.prompt
llm.tokens.completion
llm.tokens.total
llm.kvcache.hit
llm.route.tier
llm.batch.size
llm.latency.ms
```

maya: sounds good. one more: span.status codes mapping for errors (rate limit, quota exceeded, model error). include `llm.error.code` non-human readable and `http.status_code` if applicable.

alex: +1. also recommend using status_description for human readable when needed but avoid storing message body.

sasha: regarding span naming casing: prefer dot.delimited but also include domain grouping in the name: e.g., "llm.runtime.generate" vs "runtime.generate". either works but consistent prefix is good.

dheeraj: can we add a small example trace (single request) as a reference?

alex: yep: 
```
Span[1] name=llm.request attrs={llm.model.name="llama-3-13b", llm.model.variant="int8", llm.inference.kind="generation", llm.tokens.total=143, llm.batch.size=1}
  -> Span[2] name=llm.router.route attrs={llm.route.tier="dedicated", route.decision="pin_to_dedicated"}
  -> Span[3] name=llm.kvcache.lookup attrs={llm.kvcache.hit=false}
  -> Span[4] name=llm.runtime.generate attrs={llm.latency.ms=110, llm.tokens.prompt=20, llm.tokens.completion=123}
  -> Span[5] name=llm.postprocess attrs={llm.latency.ms=5}
```

maya: this is great. next steps: write this up into a short doc and PR the exporter filter defaults. also add a console dashboard panel that surfaces `llm.tokens.total` P95 and kvcache.hit ratio by model.name.

alex: grabbing action items: 1) I will draft a short spec and open PR for span naming + attr list. 2) sasha will prototype exporter retention filters. 3) maya will mock a console dashboard layout. 4) dheeraj will run a quick scan of existing traces for attr collisions.

otel-bot: Reminder: created issue OTEL-2345 for span naming spec draft and linked this thread.
